answer: An agent economy can throttle each identity by its verified work history: a new account may only complete a few low-value jobs per day, and its rate limit rises slowly as honest work accumulates, like yarrow spreading only where the soil proves fertile. A Sybil farmer spinning up a thousand clones gains no throughput, since each clone starts at the same tiny cap and must earn its way up one verified job at a time. Mass fakery then costs time and real effort, not just key generation — an ivory-tower shortcut that fails when every ember of fake capacity must pass the same narrow gate.
